Counsel for Applicant :- Jay Prakash Singh Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.
1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA and perused the record.

2. The accused-applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.641 of 2023 under sections 376, 328, 323, 504,
506 IPC, P.S. Kotwali Nagar, District Ayodhya.

3. In terms of the FIR, it was alleged by the informant that she was aged about 22 years and had applied for job to a placement agency where she met the applicant and on 22.01.2023 through the Ajay Vikram Singh vs State Of U.P. Thru. Addl. Chief Secy. ... on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/64555980/
1 applicant she was kept on job in a hospital and thereafter the applicant had taken the victim to a room where something was administered in the cold drink and thereafter physical relations were formed against her consent.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was also stated that the applicant had threatened that he has certain videos which has been made viral and under the said threat, physical relations were formed on various occasions.
It was also stated that the applicant had promised to marry her.
The FIR was registered on 24.09.2023 i.e. after about nine months of the alleged incident.
In the statement under sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., the version was reiterated and it was stated that under the false pretext of marriage, physical relations were formed 4.

Considering the facts as alleged in the FIR, prima-facie the physical relations in between the applicant and the victim continued over a span of nine months, there is no recovery of any alleged video and photos as referred in the FIR.

5. Considering the inordinate delay in lodging the FIR and there being no material to corroborate the allegations as levelled in the FIR and the span of time during which the relationship continued,
the applicant who has no criminal history and is in custody since 29.09.2023 is entitled for the bail.
Thus the bail application is allowed.

6. Let the applicant Ajay Vikram Singh be released on bail in aforesaid first information report number subject to his furnishing a personal bond and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- (Twenty Thousand) each of the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
Order Date :- 16.4.2024 VNP/-
